events.title: Roy Lichtenstein: Like New
events.what: The Lichtenstein retrospective brings together familiar Pop images and less-seen works, including recreations of four murals. An indoor art option that can pair with a walk through the Meatpacking District.
events.where: Whitney Museum · 99 Gansevoort Street
events.when: Oct 11, 2026–May 10, 2027 · closed Tuesdays; Fridays open until 10 p.m.
events.cost: Standard adult admission $30; ages 25 and under free. Check free-admission dates and reserve.
events.imageAlt: Roy Lichtenstein, Girl in Window, 1963; © Estate of Roy Lichtenstein, courtesy Whitney Museum

events.title: The Surrealist Book: Tomorrow Lives in Mirrors
events.what: Newly opened: unusual artists’ books, collage-filled sketchbooks and sculptural bindings by Surrealists including Dalí, Cahun and Unica Zürn. Explore how a book can become an artwork.
events.where: MoMA · Floor 3 · 11 West 53rd Street
events.when: Oct 4, 2026–Jan 23, 2027 · 10:30 a.m.–5:30 p.m.; Fridays until 8:30 p.m.
events.cost: Adult admission $30; special exhibitions included. NY State residents can reserve free Friday evening tickets.
events.imageAlt: Unica Zürn, Oracle and Spectacle, Book IV, 1960. MoMA; gift of Helen and Sam Zell. Photo: Ben Blackwell. © Verlag Brinkmann & Bose, Berlin.

events.title: Locating Girlhood opens at AFAM
events.where: American Folk Art Museum · 2 Lincoln Square
events.when: Oct 9–Feb 28 · Wed–Sun 11:30 a.m.–6 p.m.; closed Mon–Tue
events.cost: Free admission.
events.what: A new exhibition of roughly 100 works made by early American girls, including elaborate needlework, maps and painted objects. A compact, free art stop when you want something beyond shopping.
events.imageAlt: Needlework picture attributed to Faith Trumbull; Connecticut Museum / AFAM exhibition image

events.title: Outdoor skating at Rockefeller Center
events.when: Season open through March 27, 2027 · daily sessions; check the booking calendar
events.cost: Skating from $22; skate rental $12 extra. Prices vary by session.
events.where: Midtown · Rockefeller Center
events.what: The outdoor rink is open for the season. Reserve a 60-minute session and check the arrival instructions on your ticket; session prices and availability vary.
events.imageAlt: The Rink at Rockefeller Center at night, organizer promotional photograph

events.title: Nuulee’s Mongolian cashmere pop-up
events.what: Browse Mongolian cashmere and winter knitwear at a temporary Nolita shop. A seasonal shopping discovery; this is not a claim that you have purchased from the brand.
events.where: 173 Elizabeth Street
events.cost: Items priced individually; admission charge not listed.
events.imageAlt: Nuulee product photograph supplied by its pop-up organizer.

events.title: Brancusi: The Artist and His Studio
events.where: MoMA · 11 West 53rd Street, sixth floor
events.cost: Paid museum admission; eligible discounts and special free-entry rules vary.
events.what: A major exhibition connects Brancusi’s sculptures with his studio, photographs and films. Oct 22–24 are member previews; general visitors should plan for Oct 25 onward.
events.imageAlt: Brancusi: The Artist and His Studio — organizer or venue image

events.title: Kiku: Japanese chrysanthemums at NYBG
events.what: Chrysanthemums trained into arches, cascades and intricate traditional forms fill the Nolen Greenhouses. The Nov 7–8 highlight weekend adds crafts and taiko performances; garden travel is extra.
events.where: New York Botanical Garden · Nolen Greenhouses
events.when: Oct 31–Nov 15 · 10 a.m.–4 p.m.; highlight weekend Nov 7–8, noon–4 p.m.
events.cost: Garden ticket required; current ticket price not confirmed. Check the linked ticket options.
events.imageAlt: Trained pink and yellow chrysanthemums inside an NYBG greenhouse

events.title: Gen’ichirō Inokuma’s New York art circle
events.what: Paintings, photographs, film and letters trace Inokuma’s 20 years in New York and friendships across the city’s postwar art world. An indoor exhibition that connects art with the story of a creative neighborhood.
events.where: Japan Society · 333 East 47th Street
events.when: Through Jan 10 · Tue–Fri 11 a.m.–5 p.m.; Sat–Sun noon–6 p.m.; closed Mondays and major holidays
events.cost: $20 general / $15 students and seniors. Free admission Nov 6, 5–7 p.m.; regular hours are not free.
events.imageAlt: Gen’ichirō Inokuma in his 95th Street studio in 1960; photograph courtesy of MIMOCA

events.title: Paper Cuts: a world of zines and independent publishing
events.what: Explore independent publishing through a selection drawn from more than 600 zines and small-press works, with reading tables and a large visual installation. A quiet, creative alternative to a large museum.
events.where: Center for Book Arts · 28 West 27th Street, third floor
events.when: Through Dec 12 · Mon–Thu 11 a.m.–6 p.m.; Fri–Sat 11 a.m.–5 p.m.; closed Sunday
events.cost: Free admission; donations optional.
events.imageAlt: Zines from the first year of Paper Cuts; photo courtesy of Christopher Kardambikis

events.title: MoMA’s Contenders film season opens
events.what: MoMA’s annual film series revisits notable new releases with filmmaker conversations. Opening night pairs Obsession with a conversation between Curry Barker and Rian Johnson. Choose a specific screening from the program.
events.where: Museum of Modern Art · 11 West 53rd Street
events.when: Oct 28–Dec 17 · individual screening dates and times vary
events.cost: Film ticket required; current screening prices and availability are on the linked program.
events.imageAlt: An Obsession film still supplied by MoMA for The Contenders

events.title: Textiles become sculptures in In Fragments
events.what: Elodie Blanchard turns collected clothing, fabric and Mylar balloons into sculptural trees, vessels and expansive sewn compositions. An intimate gallery discovery for an afternoon downtown; check gallery opening hours.
events.where: Jane Lombard Gallery · 58 White Street
events.when: Oct 30–Dec 12 · Tue–Fri 10 a.m.–6 p.m.; Sat 11 a.m.–6 p.m.
events.cost: No admission charge listed; artwork purchases are optional.
events.imageAlt: Elodie Blanchard’s Corne d’abondance, 2026, photographed for Jane Lombard Gallery

events.title: Pier 17 pumpkin arch
events.where: Heineken Riverdeck · Pier 17, 89 South Street
events.cost: Free; no RSVP required.
events.what: A pumpkin-covered waterfront arch for a short fall stroll and photos. Come for the installation itself; rooftop concerts and Halloween parties are separate events.
events.imageAlt: The Seaport’s waterfront pumpkin arch in an organizer photograph

events.title: Yoshitomo Nara’s new paintings and giant heads
events.where: David Zwirner · 537 West 20th Street and 533 West 19th Street
events.when: Nov 5–Dec 12 · check gallery opening hours before visiting
events.cost: Free gallery admission.
events.what: A major New York solo presentation brings together paintings, drawings and sculptures. The 19th Street gallery holds thirteen enlarged bronze heads; the 20th Street space focuses on paintings and related works.
events.imageAlt: Artwork from Yoshitomo Nara’s exhibition, courtesy of David Zwirner

events.title: Light sculptures that bend like ribbons
events.where: Museum of Arts and Design · 2 Columbus Circle
events.when: Opens Oct 27; through Apr 4 · museum closed Mondays
events.cost: $20 general admission; seniors $16; students $14.
events.what: John Procario’s sculptural lighting explores the movement of bent wood and light. Pair the new exhibition with the museum’s other design galleries. First-Wednesday pay-what-you-wish is a special window, not everyday free admission.
events.imageAlt: John Procario’s sculptural lighting, photographed for the Museum of Arts and Design

events.title: A Louisiana love story with a surreal twist
events.where: Theater for the New City · 155 First Avenue
events.cost: $25; students/seniors $15; Sundays pay what you can.
events.what: Melanie Maria Goodreaux’s dark comedy places a dead crawfish farmer back in his own yard, where family, faith and old conflicts collide. Allow two hours for the performance.
events.imageAlt: The production’s Community Space Theater, photographed by Theater for the New City

events.title: Jewel-toned paintings at 52 Walker
events.where: 52 Walker · 52 Walker Street
events.cost: Free gallery admission.
events.what: Jem Perucchini’s Sospiro brings together luminous paintings and the first public presentation of his drawings. Renaissance imagery and African textiles inform the richly colored scenes; an intimate gallery stop rather than a museum-sized outing.
events.imageAlt: Jem Perucchini’s Sospiro, courtesy of the artist and Corvi-Mora, London

events.title: A tiny holiday chalet beside the rink
events.where: Rockefeller Center · enter from 49th Street
events.cost: Reservation ticket plus a $25 food-and-drink minimum per person; skating is separate.
events.what: Reserve a small private chalet for up to six people, with food and drinks from 5 Acres. Two digital photographs are included. The tree arrives Nov 7 and is not illuminated until Dec 2, so early visits are about the setting rather than a lit tree.
events.imageAlt: Rockefeller Center’s photograph of its holiday chalets in a previous season

events.title: Grand Central’s indoor Holiday Fair
events.where: Vanderbilt Hall · 89 East 42nd Street
events.when: Nov 9–Dec 24 · November Mon–Sat 10 a.m.–7 p.m.; Sun 11 a.m.–6 p.m. Closed Thanksgiving.
events.cost: Free to browse; purchases optional.
events.what: Browse handmade jewelry, pottery, art and gifts beneath Vanderbilt Hall’s chandeliers. The indoor setting makes it a useful cold-weather market. Hours extend near Christmas; the organizer lists the later holiday schedule.
events.imageAlt: Grand Central’s photograph of its Holiday Fair in a previous season

events.title: The Collective’s SoHo holiday market
events.where: 435 Broadway
events.cost: Free to browse; items individually priced.
events.what: An indoor holiday pop-up brings independent clothing, jewelry, candle and accessory brands together. Browse the stalls for smaller gifts, with no need to commit to a purchase or a fixed itinerary.
events.imageAlt: Shoppers browsing The Collective SoHo, photographed by the organizer

events.title: Grace Carney: To the Bone
events.where: P·P·O·W · 392 Broadway
events.cost: Free gallery admission.
events.what: New paintings use layered marks and shifting forms to explore the body and its surroundings. A compact, free contemporary-art stop that can fit around a Tribeca walk; check holiday closures before visiting.
events.imageAlt: Grace Carney artwork photographed for P·P·O·W

events.title: Queen Esther’s Songs for Unrequited Lovers
events.where: Leonard Nimoy Thalia · Symphony Space, Broadway at 95th Street
events.cost: $25–$35 before any additional checkout fees.
events.what: The singer premieres a song cycle about uneven, mistimed and unresolved love, backed by piano, bass, drums and saxophone. Her music crosses jazz, blues, country and soul; a seated listening evening in a small theater.
events.imageAlt: Queen Esther in Symphony Space’s artist photograph

events.title: Neue Galerie reopens with its masterworks
events.where: Neue Galerie · 1048 Fifth Avenue at 86th Street
events.when: Nov 12–Jan 11 · Wed–Mon 10 a.m.–6 p.m.; closed Tuesdays.
events.cost: $28 general admission; seniors $18; students and educators $15.
events.what: The museum’s 25th-anniversary display brings Austrian and German art back into its restored building, including Klimt’s Portrait of Adele Bloch-Bauer I. Galleries are still closed until November 12; this is a plan-ahead option.
events.imageAlt: Gustav Klimt’s Portrait of Adele Bloch-Bauer I, courtesy of Neue Galerie New York

events.title: DOC NYC opens with an artist’s Amazonian story
events.where: SVA Theatre · 333 West 23rd Street
events.when: Nov 11 · 6:45 p.m.; film 90 minutes, followed by a Q&A.
events.cost: $30 opening-night admission; $25 IFC Center members.
events.what: The Hummingbird Paints Fragrant Songs follows Shipibo artist Sara Flores as her paintings carry Indigenous knowledge from the Peruvian Amazon to international museums. The first screening includes a conversation with Flores and the directors.
events.imageAlt: Film still from The Hummingbird Paints Fragrant Songs, supplied by DOC NYC

events.title: The Holiday Train Show returns to NYBG
events.where: New York Botanical Garden · 2900 Southern Boulevard
events.cost: Paid All-Garden Pass; price varies by date and ticket type.
events.what: Miniature trains run through a landscape of roughly 200 New York landmarks made from botanical materials, with One Vanderbilt joining the display. Evening Holiday Train Nights begin later, on November 27.
events.imageAlt: Miniature buildings and lush planting at NYBG’s Holiday Train Show

events.title: Fall Foliage Super Hike in Prospect Park
events.where: Picnic House · West Drive and Fifth Street
events.cost: Free; registration not required.
events.what: NYC Parks Urban Park Rangers lead a walk about fall forest ecology and why leaves change color. Meet at the Picnic House; the linked listing includes the official Parks event reference.
events.imageAlt: The Picnic House in Prospect Park, photographed by Chadwick Creative Arts

events.title: Union Square’s holiday market opens
events.where: Union Square Park
events.cost: Free to browse; food and shopping extra.
events.what: Nearly 200 vendors bring crafts, gifts and seasonal food to the park. Make it a browsing outing without a shopping commitment, or start a small holiday gift list.
events.imageAlt: A shopper browsing art prints at the Union Square Holiday Market

events.title: The New York City Veterans Day Parade
events.where: Fifth Avenue · check the official route update
events.when: Nov 11 · final route and viewing times on the organizer’s page.
events.cost: Free public street viewing.
events.what: The United War Veterans Council’s annual parade honors veterans, with astronaut Suni Williams named grand marshal. Check the official viewing information before choosing a spot.
events.imageAlt: Astronaut Suni Williams, the parade’s announced grand marshal, in the organizer’s photo

events.title: Renegade Craft’s fall fair
events.where: Metropolitan Pavilion · 125 West 18th Street
events.cost: Suggested $5 donation, optional; purchases extra.
events.what: More than 200 independent artists and makers fill the pavilion with ceramics, textiles, jewelry and other design-led work. Browsing does not require buying anything.
events.imageAlt: Visitors browsing artists’ booths at Renegade Craft

events.title: Ice-skating season at Wollman Rink
events.where: Wollman Rink · Central Park near East 59th Street
events.cost: Adult admission $16 off-peak, $28 peak or $40 prime; skate rental $12. Posted prices include tax.
events.what: A seasonal open-air skate beneath the skyline. Choose a less expensive session if your schedule allows, and check the booking calendar for weather changes and the date’s price category.
events.imageAlt: An aerial evening view of skaters at Wollman Rink

events.title: Alice + Olivia’s Fifth Avenue sample sale
events.where: 260 Sample Sale · 261 Fifth Avenue
events.when: Nov 10–15 · Tue 8–8; Wed–Thu 10–8; Fri 9–8; Sat 10–8; Sun 10–5.
events.cost: Free entry; merchandise prices vary.
events.what: Browse Alice + Olivia at the organizer’s Fifth Avenue flagship. The opening day has extended hours; availability and sizing change throughout the sale.
events.imageAlt: An Alice + Olivia clothing photograph supplied for the sale

events.title: A free Reggie Dinkins screening and cast conversation
events.where: The Venue on Music Row · Hard Rock Hotel New York
events.cost: Free with RSVP; capacity is limited.
events.what: NBC100 presents an advance episode of The Fall and Rise of Reggie Dinkins followed by a conversation with cast members including Tracy Morgan and Daniel Radcliffe, moderated by Josh Horowitz.
events.imageAlt: The theater seating and stage at Hard Rock Hotel’s Venue on Music Row

events.title: The Moth and Comic Relief: Funny Story
events.where: The Town Hall · 123 West 43rd Street
events.cost: Paid tickets; current seat prices and fees vary.
events.what: Ophira Eisenberg hosts five true stories told live. The announced lineup includes Laura Benanti, Jake Cornell, Jay Jurden, Hari Kondabolu and Devon Walker.
events.imageAlt: The Town Hall’s auditorium in an archival venue photograph

events.title: Whistler on the big screen
events.where: Leonard Nimoy Thalia · Symphony Space, 250 West 95th Street
events.cost: $18 general admission, plus $2 fee; discounts available.
events.what: Exhibition on Screen explores James McNeill Whistler through the Tate exhibition, bringing his paintings and the story behind them into the cinema.
events.imageAlt: Whistler’s painting of his mother in the film distributor’s exhibition image

events.title: The Precipice: a new-musical reading
events.where: David Rubenstein Atrium · 1887 Broadway
events.cost: Free, first come first served; optional Fast Track opens Monday at noon that week.
events.what: Hear Miranda Ferriss Jones’s new musical in a staged reading with an announced cast including Laura Benanti and Lorna Courtney. Check the performance listing for current casting.
events.imageAlt: The David Rubenstein Atrium’s performance space and green wall

events.title: Luisito Gómez & Calle 107: salsa at the Atrium
events.where: David Rubenstein Atrium · 1887 Broadway
events.cost: Free, first come first served; optional Fast Track opens Monday at noon that week.
events.what: A live salsa performance and social-dance evening with Luisito Gómez & Calle 107, plus DJ Bembona. Come to listen or join the dancing; the event also offers a livestream.
events.imageAlt: Luisito Gómez in the official Lincoln Center artist portrait

events.title: The Rockettes’ Christmas Spectacular
events.where: Radio City Music Hall · 1260 Sixth Avenue
events.cost: Paid reserved seats; prices and fees vary by performance.
events.what: The new “Ring” number joins the precision dance production, with expanded immersive effects inside Radio City. Compare seat prices before booking; this is a theater outing rather than a free holiday display.
events.imageAlt: The Rockettes pose together outdoors in sparkling silver costumes.

events.title: Gingerbread NYC: The Great Borough Bake-Off
events.where: Museum of the City of New York · 1220 Fifth Avenue
events.when: Nov 6–Jan 18 during museum hours. Nov 18 closes at 2 p.m.; Nov 21 closed.
events.cost: Adult admission $23; NYC residents pay what they can with ID. Wednesday admission is free at the counter.
events.what: Explore edible interpretations of iconic New York buildings, made by bakers representing the five boroughs, and vote for a favorite. Holiday closures apply; free Wednesday admission is a specific offer, not the everyday price.
events.imageAlt: Visitors examine architectural gingerbread creations on long tables in the Museum of the City of New York.

events.title: Lightscape at Brooklyn Botanic Garden
events.where: Brooklyn Botanic Garden · 990 Washington Avenue
events.cost: Adults $39 off-peak / $44 peak, including fees; separate evening ticket.
events.what: Follow the outdoor illuminated trail through the garden. Book the date and entry window you want and dress for a long walk outside; daytime garden admission does not include this event.
events.imageAlt: Visitors walk beneath a tunnel of golden lights at Brooklyn Botanic Garden.

events.title: Bronx Zoo Holiday Lights
events.where: Bronx Zoo · 2300 Southern Boulevard
events.when: Public nights begin Nov 21; selected dates through Jan 3.
events.cost: Paid date-specific tickets; check the booking page for current prices.
events.what: Animal lanterns and illuminated trails return with a new farmyard area. The organizer says a Holiday Lights ticket allows entry from 1 p.m., so check the selected date’s daytime and evening schedule before going.
events.imageAlt: An alpaca stands beneath colorful evening lights at the Bronx Zoo.

events.title: Shine Bright at Hudson Yards
events.where: The Shops & Restaurants at Hudson Yards
events.when: Nov 16–Jan 7; Shops hours generally Mon–Sat 10 a.m.–9 p.m., Sun 11 a.m.–7 p.m.
events.cost: Free to browse the lights; shopping, dining and Vessel admission are extra.
events.what: See the Great Room’s glowing hot-air-balloon centerpiece and the seasonal lighting across Hudson Yards. A good indoor option when the weather makes an outdoor lights walk less appealing.
events.imageAlt: The illuminated balloon installation and golden lights inside Hudson Yards.

events.title: Diwali crafts and dance at the Seaport
events.where: South Street Seaport Museum · 213 Water Street
events.cost: Free; advance registration recommended.
events.what: A family-oriented afternoon with the Rubin Museum and Culture Tree: help assemble a flower-petal rangoli, make sand art and a diya-inspired candle, and join the 5–5:30 p.m. dance workshop.
events.imageAlt: Children assemble a colorful flower-petal rangoli at a Diwali celebration.

events.title: Santa’s Winter Wonderland at Watermark
events.where: Watermark · Pier 15, 78 South Street
events.when: Nov 13–Dec 27; choose an available admission or dining slot.
events.cost: General admission starts at $18; heated-glasshouse dining has separate pricing.
events.what: The waterfront venue fills with Christmas trees and seasonal decorations. General admission is an outdoor visit with hot chocolate; a heated glasshouse meal is a separate reservation, so compare the two experiences before buying.
events.imageAlt: Santa poses amid Christmas decorations at Watermark on the waterfront.

events.title: Veterans Day ceremony aboard Intrepid
events.where: Intrepid Museum · Pier 86, West 46th Street
events.cost: Included with paid museum admission.
events.what: The museum’s annual remembrance includes remarks and a wreath-laying ceremony on the Hudson. Allow time for museum entry; the ceremony being included does not mean general admission is free.
events.imageAlt: Ceremonial wreaths beside the Hudson River at the Intrepid Museum.

events.title: Harlem Holiday Lights parade
events.where: 125th Street; parade begins at Broadway
events.when: Nov 17 · 6–8:30 p.m.; announced rain date Nov 24.
events.cost: Free public parade.
events.what: Watch the illuminated floats along 125th Street. Belongó’s Fat Cats youth ensemble is among the participating musicians; check the organizer’s route and rain updates before choosing a viewing spot.
events.imageAlt: Participants gather beside a light-covered vehicle at Harlem Holiday Lights.

events.title: Opening day: Grand Central’s Holiday Train Show
events.where: New York Transit Museum Gallery · Shuttle Passage, Grand Central
events.when: Opens Nov 13; continues into February 2027, with final day not yet specified.
events.cost: Free gallery admission.
events.what: Lionel trains circle a 34-foot, two-level miniature New York, including new neighborhood buildings by Danny Cortes. Gallery hours are weekdays 10 a.m.–7:30 p.m. and weekends 10 a.m.–6 p.m.; closed major holidays. Photo shows the previous season’s display.
events.imageAlt: A family watches miniature trains in a previous season’s Transit Museum holiday display.

events.title: Grand Central Thanksgiving Market
events.where: Biltmore Room, near Track 42 · Grand Central Terminal
events.cost: Browse the public terminal; food and other purchases cost extra.
events.what: Meet Grand Central food vendors at this one-day Thanksgiving market and pick up seasonal provisions in the Biltmore Room. Browsing and buying are separate: allow a budget for any food you choose to take home.
events.imageAlt: The Grand Central Market interior, with its illuminated ceiling decoration.

events.title: Wayzgoose: a holiday letterpress evening
events.where: Bowne & Co. and Seaport Museum · 207–213 Water Street
events.cost: Tickets $15.
events.what: Pull a festive keepsake on a historic printing press, browse paper goods and enjoy light refreshments. The museum exhibitions remain open until 8:30 p.m., with a type-focused tour at 7:45 p.m.
events.imageAlt: Ink is rolled onto equipment at a historic printing press.

events.title: Make music with New York Philharmonic teaching artists
events.where: LeFrak Lobby, David Geffen Hall · 10 Lincoln Center Plaza
events.cost: Free general admission; capacity limited.
events.what: Join a collaborative music-making experience led by Philharmonic musicians and teaching artists. No prior musical training is required; check the event page for entry and any Fast Track availability.
events.imageAlt: Participants gather for a collaborative music activity at Lincoln Center.

events.title: The Jazmines: a musical-theater reading
events.where: David Rubenstein Atrium · Broadway between 62nd and 63rd Streets
events.cost: Free, first-come admission; optional free Fast Track when available.
events.what: A theatrical work with music considers the compromises imposed on brown artists trying to enter the theater industry. This is a reading, rather than a fully staged Broadway production.
events.imageAlt: A portrait supplied by Lincoln Center for The Jazmines reading.

events.title: Ju Percussion at the Atrium
events.where: David Rubenstein Atrium · Broadway at 62nd Street
events.cost: Free general admission; optional free Fast Track, subject to availability.
events.what: The Taiwan-based percussion ensemble brings a theatrical mix of Eastern and Western musical traditions to Lincoln Center. Arrive early for first-come entry; an announced performance is not a guarantee of an available seat.
events.imageAlt: The Ju Percussion ensemble poses together against a dark background.

events.title: NBC100: The Next Great Comedy
events.where: The Venue on Music Row · Hard Rock Hotel, 159 West 48th Street
events.cost: Free with RSVP; capacity limited.
events.what: Dan Goor, Luke Del Tredici and comedy performers discuss making the next NBC comedy, with a preview of Sunset P.I. Check the festival’s RSVP for the current lineup and availability. Photo shows the host hotel’s lobby.
events.imageAlt: The lobby of the Hard Rock Hotel New York, the host venue.

events.title: The Breakouts at The Stand
events.where: The Stand · 116 East 16th Street
events.when: Nov 12 at 10 p.m. or Nov 13 at 8 p.m.
events.cost: Paid tickets; current price and any minimum should be checked at booking.
events.what: A New York Comedy Festival showcase of emerging stand-ups. Pick the specific performance you want; each night has its own ticket link and lineup can change.
events.imageAlt: The red stage and seating at The Stand comedy club.

events.title: Opening day: The Photography Triennial — After Dark
events.where: Museum of the City of New York · 1220 Fifth Avenue
events.when: Opens Nov 20; ongoing exhibition, final date not announced. Museum closed Nov 21.
events.cost: Adult $23; NYC residents pay what they can with ID.
events.what: Photographers explore the city after sunset: nightlife, labor, public space and private moments. Visit the newly opened exhibition during museum hours; the museum is closed the day after opening, November 21.
events.imageAlt: Three people with martinis in a photograph featured by the Museum of the City of New York.

events.title: Meet chef Judy Joo at Chelsea Market
events.where: Pearl River Mart Foods, Chelsea Market · 75 Ninth Avenue
events.cost: Reserve a spot; books available for purchase. Admission charge not specified on the organizer page.
events.what: The chef and cookbook author signs Mukja: Let’s Eat!, her collection inspired by Korean food and pop culture. A book signing and conversation, not a promised tasting or an allergy-safe meal.
events.imageAlt: Chef Judy Joo prepares food at a kitchen counter.

events.title: Revolutionary Ink book launch
events.where: South Street Seaport Museum · 213 Water Street
events.cost: Free; RSVP requested.
events.what: Historian Mark J. Noonan discusses the New York printers who helped circulate revolutionary ideas, and the gap between democratic language and who could exercise those rights. The reception accompanies the museum’s printing-history exhibition.
events.imageAlt: The interior of Bowne & Co.’s historic printing shop.
